english.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for recurring, habitual, or colloquially emphatic ‘always’.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for something happening very often or repeatedly.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for something happening frequently or repeatedly.
This is the all-purpose casual choice when an action keeps happening, often with an annoyed tone.
Use this colloquial choice when emphasizing that something happens very frequently or seems to happen all the time.
Use this for something that keeps happening repeatedly, especially in complaints such as constantly reminding someone.
Use this colloquial choice when commonly means ‘frequently’, especially when an action happens repeatedly.
Use this when “much” means often or frequently, especially in everyday questions about repeated behavior.
Use this for repeated or constant behavior, especially in complaints such as “you are forever nagging me.”

examples.english: You always go to bed so late.

examples.english: I frequently forget to bring my keys.

examples.english: You repeatedly forget to bring your keys.
examples.jyutping: nei5 seng4 jat6 m4 gei3 dak1 daai3 so2 si4

examples.english: It often rains, so I don't feel like going out.
